description.it: Vita di frate Ginepro, il «buon giullare di Dio» compagno di san Francesco, in quindici capitoli, dalla raccolta dei Fioretti.
description.en-US: The Life of Brother Juniper, Francis’s companion and “God’s good jester”, in fifteen chapters, from the Fioretti family of texts. Italian, with the Hudleston revision of the first English translation beside it.
description.pt-BR: A Vida de frei Junípero, companheiro de São Francisco, em quinze capítulos, da família dos Fioretti.

it.editor: transcription by M. Mastrorilli, Politecnico di Bari; edition not stated (the Cesari text family)

en-US.translator: first English translation (Lady Georgiana Fullerton, 1864), revised by Dom Roger Hudleston

sources.edition: Vita di frate Ginepro, poliba.it (Wayback Machine snapshot).
sources.description: Fifteen chapters. The English of the CCEL Hudleston revision (Part II) is not imported.
sources.tierEvidence: Medieval text. The transcription (M. Mastrorilli, Politecnico di Bari, Biblioteca di Scienze del Cristianesimo, 2000-02) survives only in the Wayback Machine; it states no edition, but its biblical apparatus follows Fontes Franciscani (1995). Free in practice, edition unverified.

sources.edition: The Little Flowers of St. Francis, first English translation revised and emended by Dom Roger Hudleston (London: Burns Oates, 1926), Christian Classics Ethereal Library, flowers.txt.
sources.description: The corresponding part of the CCEL text, one chapter to a chapter of the Italian, with the chapter headings as titles. The Heritage Press introduction by Arthur Livingston (1965) is not imported.
sources.tierEvidence: Translation of 1864, revision of 1926 (Hudleston d. 1925); CCEL marks it public domain.

title.en-US: Chapter I: How brother juniper cut off the foot of a pig to give it to a sick brother
Chapter II: An instance of brother juniper's great power against the devil
Chapter III: How, by the contrivance of the devil, brother juniper was condemned to the gallows
Chapter IV: How brother juniper gave all that he had to the poor for the love of god
Chapter V: How brother juniper took certain little bells from the altar, and gave them away for the love of god
Chapter VI: How brother juniper kept silence for six months
Chapter VII: His remedy for temptations of the flesh
Chapter VIII: How brother juniper made himself contemptible for the love of god
Chapter IX: How brother juniper, in order to be despised, played at see-saw
Chapter X: How brother juniper once cooked for the brethren enough to last for a fortnight
Chapter XI: How brother juniper went one day to assisi for his own confusion
Chapter XII: How brother juniper fell into an ecstasy during the celebration of mass
Chapter XIII: Of the sorrow which brother juniper felt at the loss of his companion brother amazialbene
Chapter XIV: Of the hand which brother juniper saw in the air
Chapter XV: How st francis commanded brother leo to wash the stone
